rationale: PINS THE TWO RULED EXTENDED TYPES (`renders`, `mixes_in`) BESIDE THE CONSTRUCTS THAT MAKE EACH RULING TRUE, so neither ruling rests on an absence. EVIDENCE (whole admitted population, 1,181 .ps1/.psm1/.psd1 files over 30 repositories, script/m14/powershell-extended-census.ts -> validation/m14/measurements/powershell-extended-census.json, control PASSED): `renders` has 15 ConvertTo-Html sites in 1 file, 0 Out-GridView, 0 Show-Command and 1 XamlReader mention, against a vocabulary with 0 component symbol kinds among its 32 SymbolKinds — a serializer of objects to HTML TEXT renders no component and its target is data, not a component symbol. `mixes_in` has 273 class statements whose 50 base-list entries ARE conformance (pinned here as extends + implements), and 326 runtime member-attachment sites whose member-set argument is ALWAYS inline (script block 25, array-wrapped script block 33, string 61); the only 3 declaration-shaped hits are -Name arguments (a member's own name; Add-Type naming the type it compiles), which are not member sets. FORBID (A) is the render negative: ConvertTo-Html and [Windows.Markup.XamlReader]::Parse are the two render-sounding constructs the language actually has, and a rule keyed on the words 'html'/'markup' or on a static [T]::Parse call would emit `renders` here. FORBID (B) is the mixin negative: Add-Member and Update-TypeData attach a member to a VALUE or a TYPE NAME at runtime with the member set inline, which is mutation of an object rather than a declaration composing a named member set into a type. FIRE rows are the same conformance constructors the ruling leans on, so a lane that silenced them would fail this fixture.

expectRelationships.comment: FIRE (1) — the FIRST name in the base list is the superclass. This is the construct a mixes_in reading would have to steal, and it is `extends`.
FIRE (1) — the remaining names in the base list are interfaces: conformance declared, which is exactly what a mixin does NOT do.
FORBID (A) read the RIGHT way — a serializer INVOCATION is a call. It turns objects into HTML text; it renders no component.
FORBID (A) read the RIGHT way — a static [T]::Parse call constructs UI from XAML TEXT. The thing rendered is a document, not a declared component.
FORBID (B) read the RIGHT way — attaching a member to an object VALUE is a cmdlet call, not a declaration composing a member set.
FORBID (B) read the RIGHT way — attaching a member to a TYPE NAME at runtime is a cmdlet call; the object it extends is not a declaration that composes anything.
FIRE (2) — the ordinary declared-callee call the file's other edges hang from

expectRelationshipCount.comment: THE RULING, PINNED AS A COUNT. This file contains both render-sounding constructs the language has (an object-to-HTML serializer and a XAML reader that constructs UI elements). Neither target is a component symbol, and the vocabulary has no component symbol kind. A rule keyed on a command name, on 'markup'/'html', or on a static [T]::Parse call would fire here.

THE SECOND RULING, PINNED AS A COUNT. This file contains both member-attachment cmdlets (Add-Member against a value, Update-TypeData against a type name) plus a class base list. The base list is conformance (extends/implements above) and the attachments are runtime mutation with inline script blocks; no declaration composes a named member set into a type.
EXACTLY one — the first base-list name. A rule that read every base-list entry as a superclass would make this 2 and delete the interfaces distinction.
EXACTLY one — the interface entry. Together with the extends count this pins the positional split the class header forces.

forbidRelationships.comment: FORBID (A) — no renders at all, from any endpoint. A corpus-zero ruling must not be reachable by a shape the language really has, and this file carries the two shapes that look closest.

a static [T]::Parse call is a CALL — the analyzer emits it as such; it is not a render of the thing it parses
FORBID (B) — no mixes_in at all, from any endpoint. Member attachment at runtime is not a declaration-level composition.
the specific wrong edge Update-TypeData invites: Widget is the HOST the member is attached to, and the member set is an inline script block, not the class method Describe
the conformance relation restated as a mixin — the exact relabel this fixture refuses; it is `extends`
as above for the interface: it is `implements`
